issue_context.title: WebGPU Node system extremely slow startup
issue_context.body:
### Description

Hi, I started exploring webgpu in threejs, however the startup time is just insane,
in the following scene with 4 materials, the scene only shows up after 1.6 seconds.
 
After a bit a profiling, it seems like the culprit is the WGSLNodeBuilder: each material has about 1000 nodes to construct which takes forever (about 400+ms per material). 

https://threejs.org/examples/?q=webgpu#webgpu_clearcoat

Any fixes on the table? Is this going to be a limitation of the node system

At the moment it is not really usable beyond small prototypes but even then having the wait multiple seconds for those node materials to build is definitely not ideal


### Reproduction steps

1. Open https://threejs.org/examples/?q=webgpu#webgpu_clearcoat
2. Profile in the dev console


### Screenshots

![Screenshot 2023-09-21 165039](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/87069099/556359cd-5bcb-4030-9b66-3abfe0efbc45)


### Version

156

### Device

Desktop

### Browser

Chrome

### OS

Windows
comments: Maybe the shader compiler on Windows is super slow compared to the one in MacOS?
I had `~0.6` on my laptop with Windows and Ryzen 7 processor, less than `1 ms` to render/compile the first frame.
In any case, there is a strange behavior, as the frame is taking a long time to appear. I will analyze this more carefully.

On my side, the screen stays black for about 2 seconds before displaying the first frame which is not the case when using webgl or even babylon webgpu. I have a solid pc with a nvidia 3090 and the I am having the exact same issue on my macbook (actually worse..). 

The performance issue is happening inside the WGSLNodeBuilder when the materials are being created. I do not believe that this is related to webgpu api as I do not have such issue with babylon nor emscripten. 

As for the benchmark, the load is spread out across multiple frames so it's easier to visualize in the profiler, here is a zoomed out version of the profiler on one of the material during startup (when the page is loaded or material created for the first time):

![Screenshot 2023-09-21 201738](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/87069099/ab42c953-9e79-4d6a-b7f6-4e8a904fc02e)

As you can see most of the compute is going toward this traverse method in the `core/Node.js`
```js


	traverse( callback, replaceNode = null ) {

		callback( this, replaceNode );

		for ( const { childNode, replaceNode } of this.getChildren() ) {

			childNode.traverse( callback, replaceNode );

		}

	}
```
	
As for JS benchmark in the console sure:
```

```
@sunag  Any way to reopen this issue?

> @sunag Any way to reopen this issue?

Yes, I think it's worth analyzing all these points first.

What is suspicious is that these slow `traverse`s all happen in `VarNode.assign()`. I think what we should do is fix it so that it works in runtime instead of compile-time (as I suggested in https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/26795#issuecomment-1723771178, for a completely different reason). We can also remove `replaceNode` then.

I can file a PR for that.

The exact reason for the slowness is maybe that these VarNodes have a tremendous amount of subnodes -- and `VarNode.assign()` must (in the current implementation) check them all.
If we can replace these `VarNode.assign` with `stack.assign` is better, it follows flow, and there is no need to `traverse`.

I think we can close this after https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/26881 is merged.

@alienself Does the performance become better for you?
[This update](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/26885) had more impact on my tests.

@sunag @LeviPesin performance did improve by around 100ms, kudos on this improvement for sure!

However is this as good as it gets? 
We went from building each material node from about 400ms to now around 280ms, so the lag is still clearly visible since the time to first canvas paint depends heavily on the number of material to build. 

If you have 50 materials that's 280ms * 50 = 14 seconds (oouch!)

Have you though about adding a stress test scene for node materials with many materials created when the page loads as well as instantiated at runtime for instance at the press of a button?

![Screenshot 2023-10-02 092808](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/87069099/d9e8ff6f-aa7b-48f4-aa5d-19563bf3aa8c)
Are you sure you really are testing the latest version? There should not be `assign-traverse-traverse-...` blocks, they were removed in https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/26881.

> If you have 50 materials that's 280ms * 50 = 14 seconds (ouch!)

This logic should not happen, if you create 50 materials and only change the color or texture for example, the cache system must reuse the `NodeBuilder` and the `GPU Program` and this process would only happen once. Compile time should decrease every time new material is created as the cache increases.

Approach like https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/26889 will do the same thing at a function level.

> Have you though about adding a stress test scene for node materials with many materials created when the page loads as well as instantiated at runtime for instance at the press of a button?

Yes, a good idea.

> There should not be assign-traverse-traverse-... blocks, they were removed in https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/26881.

Yeah, that's probably it, I did a closer test and placed the `performance.now()` code inside `NodeBuilder.build()`.

In my tests, previously I had an average of `180 ms` and now `14 ms`.
